newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NEW INTEREST IN MARK ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MARKET.
newsitem.headline: NEW INTEREST IN MARK ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MARKET.

text.p: The mark was the focus of trade on the currency futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday after it found new strength against the dollar on the spot market, dealers said.
The Budapest Stock Exchange forex futures market saw no trade and no price changes.
"Both the dollar and the mark are generating interest since the government announced a fall in the crawling peg devaluation rate for the forint," said BCE trader Mihaly Eotvos of OTP Forex.

Last weekend the government announced that on April 1 it would reduce the forint's crawling peg devaluator against a currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar to 1.1 percent per month from 1.2 percent.
The mark accounted for almost half the BCE's moderate 5.648 billion forints' turnover, with the dollar and yen also featuring.
"There's still a feeling that the yen is going to weaken against the forint in the longer term," said Eotvos.
The mark only registered slight changes on the BCE market, falling five fillers to 112.25 forints for September and rising 10 fillers to 116.1 for December.
The dollar rose 33 fillers to 185.07 forints for its most popular month, June, and fell 15 fillers to 190.45 forints for September.
The central bank midday spot fix for the two currencies was 103.79 for the mark, unchanged from Tuesday and 177.43 for the dollar, down from 177.03.
